recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: dependency/toolchain/runtime/native/embedded change needs a new binary; S5 keeps the listening socket and transfers state unchanged (state schema identical)

goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits

S6 blockers (14): github.com/gotify/server/v3: new program entry point; github.com/gotify/server/v3/api/stream.API.Handle: new long-running goroutine; github.com/gotify/server/v3/api/stream.client.startWriteHandler: new long-running goroutine; github.com/gotify/server/v3/plugin.NewManager: new long-running goroutine; github.com/gotify/server/v3/plugin/example/clock: new program entry point; ... and 9 more
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 390 functions
42 patched functions are in package main; a Go plugin cannot import package main, so hotpatchgen must relocate them into an importable package
type information is partial (359/359 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
